The DLT homography fails due to collinearity of landmarks, rendering it non-invertible. Tracklet association operates under synthetic data only, making its performance meaningless. Coverage shells are hardcoded or self-referential, lacking external validation. These primitives form an algebraic framework that cannot be evaluated without real-world input. The system exhibits a fundamental epistemic gap: all metrics are computed but none reflect reality. This leads to a retrocausal paradox where outputs are generated but not grounded in observation. The failure mode is not algorithmic but ontological—no data exists to confirm any computation.
